units.text: The 1969 Vienna Convention applies only to treaties between sovereign states, as stated in Article 1.

citations.title: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties - Wikipedia

judgement.reason: Passages state Article 1 restricts the convention to written treaties between states, but also note Article 2 and Article 5 apply to treaties between states and intergovernmental organizations, so the absolute 'only' claim is not fully supported.

units.text: Article 1 of the Vienna Convention excludes treaties involving non-state actors such as international organizations.

citations.title: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties - Wikipedia

judgement.reason: The passage explicitly states that Article 1 restricts the VCLT to treaties between states, excluding treaties involving international organizations.

units.text: The Convention does not apply to treaties between states and international organizations, confirming its limitation to state-to-state agreements.

citations.title: Oxford Public International Law: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties (1969)

judgement.reason: The passages explicitly state the VCLT does not apply to treaties between a State and an international organization, which are instead covered by the 1986 Vienna Convention, and that it applies only to treaties concluded by States.

units.text: Private corporations are non-state actors and are not included in the scope of treaties governed by the Vienna Convention.

citations.title: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties - Wikipedia

judgement.reason: The passages state the VCLT governs treaties between states and excludes non-state actors, giving international organizations as an example, but they do not mention private corporations or explicitly classify them as non-state actors.

units.text: The claim that the Convention applies to treaties between states and private corporations is contradicted by its explicit state-only limitation.

citations.title: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties - Wikipedia
Oxford Public International Law: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties (1969)

judgement.reason: The passages state the VCLT defines treaties as between states and excludes non-state actors, which includes private corporations, thereby contradicting any claim that it applies to state–private corporation treaties.
